# contentful_personal_access_token (Resource)

Manages a Contentful Personal Access Token. Changing `name`, `scopes`, or `expires_in` requires a new token; Terraform revokes the old token during replacement. Changing only `timeouts` preserves the existing token. Destroy revokes the token.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "contentful_personal_access_token" "this" {
  name       = "management access token"
  scopes     = ["content_management_manage"]
  expires_in = 90 * 24 * 60 * 60
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the token. Changing this value replaces the resource.
- `scopes` (List of String) Access granted to the token: `content_management_read` for read access or `content_management_manage` for read and write access. Changing this value replaces the resource.

### Optional

- `expires_in` (Number) Token lifetime in seconds. Omit it on creation for a token without automatic expiry. Changing the duration replaces the token. Import leaves it unset even when the token has an expiry date.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `expires_at` (String) RFC 3339 timestamp when the token expires.
- `id` (String) System ID of the personal access token. This is distinct from the secret `token` value.
- `revoked_at` (String) RFC 3339 timestamp when the token was revoked.
- `token` (String, Sensitive) The access token for the Content Management API. Contentful returns it only on creation; Terraform retains the known value in state during later refreshes. Import cannot recover the token and leaves this attribute null.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) Duration for the complete operation, including retries, for example `30s` or `5m`. Defaults to `2m`.
- `delete` (String) Includes retries and uses the duration saved in state (default `2m`, minimum provider timeout `10s`).
- `read` (String) Includes retries and uses the duration saved in state (default `2m`, minimum provider timeout `10s`).

## Import

To keep an existing token, match its `name` and `scopes` and omit `expires_in`. Contentful returns the expiry timestamp in `expires_at`. Setting `expires_in`, even to the original duration, plans a replacement that revokes the imported token. Import cannot recover the secret `token` value.

### By identity (Terraform 1.12 or later)

```terraform
import {
  identity = {
    id = var.id
  }
  to = contentful_personal_access_token.this
}
```

### By ID (Terraform 1.5 or later)

```terraform
import {
  id = var.id
  to = contentful_personal_access_token.this
}
```

### From the command line

```shell
terraform import contentful_personal_access_token.this "$CONTENTFUL_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN_ID"
```
